idiom_name: withFrameNanos inside a coroutine / Choreographer.FrameCallback with a list walk
implementation_notes: Kotlin's hook is a plain method (fun update(dt: Float)) on any class, the collection is a list, and the frame comes from the platform: Compose's MonotonicFrameClock 'Provides a time source for display frames and the ability to perform an action on the next frame' and withFrameNanos 'Suspends until a new frame is requested, immediately invokes onFrame with the frame time in nanoseconds'; on classic Android the Choreographer.FrameCallback fires 'when a new display frame is being rendered' but 'the callback runs once then is automatically removed', so it must re-post each frame. What replaces the classic structure: coroutines and the platform frame clock replace the driver (no thread, no base class) and a list walk inside the frame block replaces the entity manager; suspend-based frames also flatten the step's control flow, which is Kotlin's answer to the pattern's explicit-resume-state cost.
pitfalls: withFrameNanos needs a MonotonicFrameClock in the coroutine context: outside Compose/Android (headless tests) it throws IllegalStateException - use TestMonotonicFrameClock or a plain loop.
Choreographer callbacks are one-shot and run on the Looper thread they were posted from; forgetting to re-post silently stops every update.
Nanosecond frame timestamps spike after a pause or debugger stop: clamp dt and never confuse frameTimeNanos with wall-clock time.
Removing dead entities inside the walk throws ConcurrentModificationException or skips entries; remove after the loop (removeAll) or iterate by index.
